shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः । कुम्भयोनिर्मिहातेजा राममेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ | kumbhayonirmihātejā rāmametaduvāca ha || 7.2.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard those words of the great-souled Raghava, the pitcher-born sage of mighty splendor spoke thus to Rama.

shlokas.sanskrit: शृणु राम कथावृत्तं तस्य तेजोबलं महत् । जघान शत्रून्येनासौ न च वध्यः स शत्रुभिः ।। 7.2.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śṛṇu rāma kathāvṛttaṃ tasya tejobalaṃ mahat | jaghāna śatrūnyenāsau na ca vadhyaḥ sa śatrubhiḥ || 7.2.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Hear, Rama, the tale of his great splendor and strength, by which he slew his enemies, while he himself could not be slain by his foes.

shlokas.sanskrit: तावत्ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव । वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते ।। 7.2.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tāvatte rāvaṇasyedaṃ kulaṃ janma ca rāghava | varapradānaṃ ca tathā tasmai dattaṃ bravīmi te || 7.2.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: So now, O Raghava, I shall tell you of Ravana's lineage and his birth, and likewise of the boon that was granted to him.

shlokas.sanskrit: पुरा कृतयुगे राम प्रजापतिसुतः प्रभुः । पुलस्त्यो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षादिव पितामहः ।। 7.2.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: purā kṛtayuge rāma prajāpatisutaḥ prabhuḥ | pulastyo nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣādiva pitāmahaḥ || 7.2.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: In olden times, in the Krita age, O Rama, there was a lord, the son of Prajapati, a brahmin-sage named Pulastya, who was like the Grandsire (Brahma) himself made manifest.

shlokas.sanskrit: नानुकीर्त्या गुणास्तस्य धर्मतः शीलतस्तथा । प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः ।। 7.2.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nānukīrtyā guṇāstasya dharmataḥ śīlatastathā | prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṃ śakyaṃ hi nāmataḥ || 7.2.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: His virtues, in righteousness and in conduct, cannot be fully recounted; it is enough that he can be named simply as the son of Prajapati.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रजापतिसुतत्वेन देवानां वल्लभो हि सः । हृष्टः सर्वस्य लोकस्य गुणैः शुभ्रैर्महामतिः ।। 7.2.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: prajāpatisutatvena devānāṃ vallabho hi saḥ | hṛṣṭaḥ sarvasya lokasya guṇaiḥ śubhrairmahāmatiḥ || 7.2.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: By his being the son of Prajapati he was indeed beloved of the gods; that great-minded one, delighting all the world by his pure virtues, was a joy to all.

shlokas.sanskrit: स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः । तृणविन्द्वाश्रमं गत्वा न्यवसन्मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.2.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ | tṛṇavindvāśramaṃ gatvā nyavasanmunipuṅgavaḥ || 7.2.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And that bull among sages, drawn by his devotion to dharma, went to the hermitage of Trinabindu on the slope of the great mountain Meru, and dwelt there.

shlokas.sanskrit: तपस्तेपे स धर्मात्मा स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः । गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tapastepe sa dharmātmā svādhyāyaniyatendriyaḥ | gatvāśramapadaṃ tasya vighnaṃ kurvanti kanyakāḥ || 7.2.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That righteous one, his senses restrained and devoted to the recitation of the Vedas, performed austerities there; but maidens, coming to his hermitage, would disturb him.

shlokas.sanskrit: देवपन्नगकन्याश्च राजर्षितनयाश्च याः । क्रीडन्त्यो ऽप्सरसश्चैव तं देशमुपपेदिरे ।। 7.2.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: devapannagakanyāśca rājarṣitanayāśca yāḥ | krīḍantyo 'psarasaścaiva taṃ deśamupapedire || 7.2.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Daughters of the gods and of the serpents, and the daughters of royal sages, and apsarases sporting about, would come to that place.

shlokas.sanskrit: सर्वर्तुषृपभोग्यत्वाद्रम्यत्वात्काननस्य च । नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sarvartuṣṛpabhogyatvādramyatvātkānanasya ca | nityaśastāstu taṃ deśaṃ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ || 7.2.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Because the woodland could be enjoyed in every season and was so delightful, those maidens would constantly go to that place and play there.

shlokas.sanskrit: देशस्य रमणीयत्वात्पुलस्त्यो यत्र स द्विजः । गायन्त्यो वादयन्त्यश्च लासयन्त्यस्तथैव च । मुनेस्तपस्विनस्तस्य विघ्नं चक्रुरनिन्दिताः ।। 7.2.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: deśasya ramaṇīyatvātpulastyo yatra sa dvijaḥ | gāyantyo vādayantyaśca lāsayantyastathaiva ca | munestapasvinastasya vighnaṃ cakruraninditāḥ || 7.2.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Because of the loveliness of the place where Pulastya, that twice-born sage, dwelt, those blameless maidens, singing and playing instruments and dancing, caused a disturbance to that ascetic sage.

shlokas.sanskrit: अथ क्रुद्धो महातेजा व्याजहार महामुनिः । या मे दर्शनमागच्छेत्सा गर्भं धारयिष्यति ।। 7.2.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: atha kruddho mahātejā vyājahāra mahāmuniḥ | yā me darśanamāgacchetsā garbhaṃ dhārayiṣyati || 7.2.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the great-souled sage of mighty splendor, growing angry, declared: "Whichever woman comes within my sight shall conceive a child."

shlokas.sanskrit: तास्तु सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्य वाक्यं महात्मनः । ब्रह्मशापभयाद्भीतास्तं देशं नोपचक्रमुः ।। 7.2.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tāstu sarvāḥ pratiśrutya tasya vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ | brahmaśāpabhayādbhītāstaṃ deśaṃ nopacakramuḥ || 7.2.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Now all of them, having heard the word of that great-souled one, and being afraid out of dread of the brahmin's curse, did not approach that place.

shlokas.sanskrit: तृणबिन्दोस्तु राजर्षेस्तनया न शृणोति तत् ।। 7.2.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tṛṇabindostu rājarṣestanayā na śṛṇoti tat || 7.2.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: But the daughter of the royal sage Trinabindu did not hear of it.

shlokas.sanskrit: गत्वाश्रमपदं तत्र विचचार सुनिर्भया । न सापश्यत्स्थिता तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् ।। 7.2.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: gatvāśramapadaṃ tatra vicacāra sunirbhayā | na sāpaśyatsthitā tatra kāñcidabhyāgatāṃ sakhīm || 7.2.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Going to that hermitage, she wandered about there quite fearlessly, and she did not see standing there any companion who had come along with her.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मिन्काले महातेजाः प्राजापत्यो महानृषिः । स्वाध्यायमकरोत्तत्र तपसा भावितः स्वयम् ।। 7.2.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasminkāle mahātejāḥ prājāpatyo mahānṛṣiḥ | svādhyāyamakarottatra tapasā bhāvitaḥ svayam || 7.2.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: At that time the great-splendored son of Prajapati, the mighty sage, exalted by his own austerities, was reciting the Veda there.

shlokas.sanskrit: सा तु वेदश्रुतिं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा वै तपसो निधिम् । अभवत्पाण्डुदेहा सा सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा ।। 7.2.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sā tu vedaśrutiṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā vai tapaso nidhim | abhavatpāṇḍudehā sā suvyañjitaśarīrajā || 7.2.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And she, hearing that recitation of the Veda and beholding that treasure-house of asceticism, became pale of body, with the marks of pregnancy plainly showing upon her.

shlokas.sanskrit: वभूव च समुद्विग्ना दृष्ट्वा तद्दोषमात्मनः । इदं मे किन्त्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वा ऽ ऽश्रमे स्थिता ।। 7.2.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vabhūva ca samudvignā dṛṣṭvā taddoṣamātmanaḥ | idaṃ me kintviti jñātvā piturgatvā ' 'śrame sthitā || 7.2.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And she became greatly agitated, seeing that affliction in herself; wondering "What is this that has befallen me?" she went and stood in her father's hermitage.

shlokas.sanskrit: तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतां तृणविन्दुरथाब्रवीत् । किं त्वमेतत्त्वसदृशं धारयस्यात्मनो वपुः ।। 7.2.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtāṃ tṛṇavindurathābravīt | kiṃ tvametattvasadṛśaṃ dhārayasyātmano vapuḥ || 7.2.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Seeing her in that condition, Trinabindu then said: "Why is it that you bear upon yourself this body so unlike your own?"

shlokas.sanskrit: सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योवाच तपोधनम् । न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम् ।। 7.2.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṃ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam | na jāne kāraṇaṃ tāta yena me rūpamīdṛśam || 7.2.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the maiden, distressed, folding her hands in reverence, said to that one rich in austerities: "I do not know the reason, father, by which my form has become like this.

shlokas.sanskrit: किं तु पूर्वं गतास्म्येका महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं दिव्यमन्वेष्टुं स्वसखीजनम् ।। 7.2.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kiṃ tu pūrvaṃ gatāsmyekā maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ | pulastyasyāśramaṃ divyamanveṣṭuṃ svasakhījanam || 7.2.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "But formerly I went alone to the divine hermitage of the great sage Pulastya, whose soul was purified, in search of my own female companions."

shlokas.sanskrit: न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् । रूपस्य तु विपर्यासं दृष्ट्वा त्रासादिहागता ।। 7.2.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na ca paśyāmyahaṃ tatra kāñcidabhyāgatāṃ sakhīm | rūpasya tu viparyāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā trāsādihāgatā || 7.2.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "And there I did not see any of my companions who had come; rather, beholding the disfigurement of their appearance, I came here out of fear."

shlokas.sanskrit: तृणबिन्दुस्तु राजर्षिस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः । ध्यानं विवेश तच्चापि ह्यपश्यदृषिकर्मजम् ।। 7.2.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tṛṇabindustu rājarṣistapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ | dhyānaṃ viveśa taccāpi hyapaśyadṛṣikarmajam || 7.2.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Now the royal sage Trinabindu, whose radiance was kindled by his austerities, entered into meditation, and he perceived that this too was wrought by the sage's deed.

shlokas.sanskrit: स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । गृहीत्वा तनयां गत्वा पुलस्त्यमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.2.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa tu vijñāya taṃ śāpaṃ maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ | gṛhītvā tanayāṃ gatvā pulastyamidamabravīt || 7.2.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And he, recognizing that it was the curse of the great sage whose soul was purified, took his daughter and went to Pulastya, and spoke these words to him:

shlokas.sanskrit: भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम् । भिक्षां प्रतिगृहाणेमां महर्षे स्वयमुद्यताम् ।। 7.2.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bhagavaṃstanayāṃ me tvaṃ guṇaiḥ svaireva bhūṣitām | bhikṣāṃ pratigṛhāṇemāṃ maharṣe svayamudyatām || 7.2.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Reverend one, accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her own virtues, as alms, O great sage—she who of her own accord has come forward to offer herself."

shlokas.sanskrit: तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य श्रम्यमाणेन्द्रियस्य ते । शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.2.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tapaścaraṇayuktasya śramyamāṇendriyasya te | śuśrūṣaṇaparā nityaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.2.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "For you who are engaged in the practice of austerities, whose senses grow weary, she will ever be devoted to your service—of this there is no doubt."

shlokas.sanskrit: तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षिं धार्मिकं तदा । जिघृक्षुरब्रवीत्कन्यां बाढमित्येव स द्विजः ।। 7.2.27 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājarṣiṃ dhārmikaṃ tadā | jighṛkṣurabravītkanyāṃ bāḍhamityeva sa dvijaḥ || 7.2.27 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, to the royal sage who spoke that speech, the righteous twice-born one, desiring to receive the maiden, said only, "So be it."

shlokas.sanskrit: दत्त्वा स तु यथान्यायं स्वमाश्रमपदं गतः । सापि तत्रावसत्कन्या तोषयन्ती पतिं गुणैः ।। 7.2.28 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dattvā sa tu yathānyāyaṃ svamāśramapadaṃ gataḥ | sāpi tatrāvasatkanyā toṣayantī patiṃ guṇaiḥ || 7.2.28 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having given her away according to custom, he returned to his own hermitage; and that maiden too dwelt there, pleasing her husband with her virtues.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्यास्तु शीलवृत्ताभ्यां तुतोष मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.29 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasyāstu śīlavṛttābhyāṃ tutoṣa munipuṅgavaḥ | prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.2.29 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The bull among sages was gratified by her conduct and character; and that one of great splendor, well pleased, spoke this word:

shlokas.sanskrit: परितुष्टो ऽस्मि सुश्रोणि गुणानां सम्पदा भृशम् । तस्माद्देवि ददाम्यद्य पुत्रमात्मसमं तव ।। 7.2.30 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: parituṣṭo 'smi suśroṇi guṇānāṃ sampadā bhṛśam | tasmāddevi dadāmyadya putramātmasamaṃ tava || 7.2.30 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I am exceedingly content, fair-hipped lady, with the wealth of your virtues; therefore, O goddess, this day I grant you a son equal to myself."

shlokas.sanskrit: उभयोर्वंशकर्तारं पौलस्त्य इति विश्रुतम् । यस्मात्तु विश्रुतो वेदस्त्वयैषो ऽध्ययतो मम ।। 7.2.31 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ubhayorvaṃśakartāraṃ paulastya iti viśrutam | yasmāttu viśruto vedastvayaiṣo 'dhyayato mama || 7.2.31 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "He shall be the founder of the lineage of both of us, renowned as Paulastya; and because the Veda was heard by you as I recited it,"

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः । एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ।। 7.2.32 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasmātsa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ | evamuktā tu sā devī prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā || 7.2.32 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "therefore he shall be named Vishravas—of this there is no doubt." Thus addressed, that goddess, with her inmost soul rejoicing,

shlokas.sanskrit: अचिरेणैव कालेनासूत विश्रवसं सुतम् । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यशोधर्मसमन्वितम् ।। 7.2.33 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: acireṇaiva kālenāsūta viśravasaṃ sutam | triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ yaśodharmasamanvitam || 7.2.33 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: in but a short time bore the son Vishravas, renowned throughout the three worlds and endowed with glory and righteousness.

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रुतिमान्समदर्शी च व्रताचाररतस्तथा । पितेव तपसा युक्तो ह्यभवद्विश्रवा मुनिः ।। 7.2.34 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śrutimānsamadarśī ca vratācāraratastathā | piteva tapasā yukto hyabhavadviśravā muniḥ || 7.2.34 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Possessed of sacred learning, of impartial vision, and devoted to the practice of vows, the sage Vishravas became, like his father, joined to austerity.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः ।। 2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ || 2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the second canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana of Valmiki, the first of poems, composed by the sage.
